scenes.heading: End-of-year exam technique
scenes.sub: Turn what you know into marks
scenes.say: Your end-of-year exam covers Units 3 and 4 together. Good technique won't replace understanding, but it stops you losing marks you've already earned.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Players warm up and hear the game plan before the first bounce
scenes.science: Use reading time to scan the paper and plan your order
scenes.breaks: in footy the opposition reacts to your plan, but an exam paper doesn't change, so planning time is never wasted.
scenes.say: Footy players don't just run out and start kicking. They warm up, look over the ground and listen to the game plan. Reading time is your warm-up: scan the whole paper, read the long scenario questions first, and spot the easy wins.

scenes.heading: Multiple-choice strategies
points: Answer it yourself before the options
Estimate to check the size of the answer
scenes.say: For multiple choice, cover the options and answer it yourself first. Underline words like not, most and least. Many distractors are built on common errors, so eliminate them, and estimate to check the size of the answer. Never leave one blank.

scenes.heading: Show your working: F S U
steps: Units and sig figs on the answer
scenes.say: Showing working is like keeping your receipts. Write the formula, substitute with units, then give the answer with units and the right significant figures. Assessors can award method marks and consequential marks, but only for what they can see.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: 25.00 mL of HCl reacts exactly with 21.40 mL of 0.1000 mol L⁻¹ NaOH. Find the concentration of the HCl.
scenes.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide are concentration times volume in litres: two point one four zero times ten to the minus three. The ratio is one to one, so divide by zero point zero two five zero zero litres. The acid is zero point zero eight five six zero molar.
scenes.caption: Moles of NaOH = c × V in litres: 2.140 × 10⁻³ mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so divide by 0.02500 L. The acid is 0.08560 mol L⁻¹.

scenes.heading: Weak vs strong explanation
scenes.say: Use chemical terms. 'The particles move faster, so it's quicker' is weak. A strong answer says the particles collide more often and, more importantly, a greater proportion of collisions have at least the activation energy.

scenes.heading: Protect your marks
points: Timed past exams and an error log
scenes.say: Before leaving any equation, check it's balanced, has states, and shows electrons in half-equations. Answer the command word. In the final weeks, do timed past exams and keep an error log. And check the current VCAA exam specifications for the exact format.

points: Only what you show can be marked
scenes.say: Quick recap. Read the long questions first. Answer multiple choice before looking at the options. Show formula, substitution and units. And remember: the assessor can only mark what they can see. Now try the practice questions!
